item.mechanism: Mn dissolution acts as a sacrificial mechanism that hinders Cr dissolution by establishing a Mn/MnF2 redox buffer in the salt, making Cr thermodynamically noble relative to the salt potential.
item.operating_conditions: Exposure to molten FLiBe salt at 700 °C for 1000 hours
item.supporting_observation: The HEA lost significantly lower amount of Cr to the salt compared to 316 H stainless steel, while Mn concentration in the salt increased significantly (from 4 to 349 ppm).
item.scope_limits: The authors note this mechanism relies on high temperature (700 °C) where Mn diffusivity is significantly increased; it is not successful in aqueous systems at low temperatures due to limited diffusivity.
item.alternatives_considered: Conventional corrosion where Cr is the most vulnerable element and leaches out, or where Mn concentration is low/non-existent.
quotes: The dissolution of Mn is governed by the presence of the more noble metallic impurities in the molten salt
The combination of lower standard Gibbs free energy and high diffusion coefficient of Mn relative to Cr, led to the higher dissolution rate of Mn in the salt that hinder the dissolution of Cr.
At this potential, the Cr becomes a noble element with respect to the salt, and Cr dissolution would not be thermodynamically favorable.

item.mechanism: Thermal exposure at 700 °C causes phase instability leading to the precipitation of a Cr-rich BCC phase (Cr67Fe13Mn18.5Ni1.5) from the FCC solid solution.
item.operating_conditions: Thermal exposure at 700 °C for 1000 hours (annealing/corrosion test)
item.supporting_observation: Bulk XRD patterns showed a new precipitate phase, and SEM-EDS revealed needle-shaped Cr-rich particles precipitating in the near-surface and bulk regions.
item.scope_limits: The authors state this phase separation was not observed in previous studies because those tests were performed at lower temperatures or for shorter times than required for separation.
item.alternatives_considered: The hypothesis that HEAs maintain a single-phase solid solution due to high entropy of mixing and sluggish diffusion.
quotes: Thermal exposure at 700 °C for 1000 hours also led to the precipitation of an additional BCC phase Cr 67 Fe 13 Mn 18.5 Ni 1.5 , which was confirmed by CALPHAD predictions.
Needle-shaped Cr-rich particles were found to precipitate and bulk XRD patterns showed that a new precipitate phase was formed after the corrosion/annealing process

item.mechanism: Mn dissolution occurs preferentially over Cr due to the lower standard Gibbs free energy of formation of MnF2 compared to CrF2.
item.system: Cr18Mn27Fe27.5Ni27.5 high entropy alloy (HEA) and 316 H stainless steel
item.operating_conditions: Exposure to molten FLiBe salt at 700 °C for 1000 hours
item.supporting_observation: Trace elemental analysis showed Mn concentration in the salt increased to 349 ppm for the HEA, while Cr concentration remained nearly unchanged compared to the reference steel.
item.scope_limits: This thermodynamic preference applies to molten fluoride salts; the authors note that in aqueous solutions, Mn is not necessarily the most active element.
item.alternatives_considered: The possibility that Cr dissolution is the primary degradation mechanism in fluoride salts.
quotes: These results may be explained by the lower standard Gibbs free energy of formation of MnF 2 compared to CrF 2 , as shown in Fig. 8 , which suggests that Mn would tend to dissolve in molten fluoride salt rather than Cr
The dissolution of Mn is governed by the presence of the more noble metallic impurities in the molten salt
This indicates that Mn may act as a sacrificial element to protect Cr from dissolution in molten fluoride salts since it has lower free energy of formation

item.mechanism: The precipitation of Cr-rich BCC phases is driven by the depletion of Mn from the alloy matrix, which alters the local thermodynamic stability and phase fractions.
item.operating_conditions: Exposure to molten FLiBe salt at 700 °C for 1000 hours
item.supporting_observation: CALPHAD calculations predicted that as Mn diffuses out, the BCC phase fraction decreases from 3.7 at.% to 0.1 at.% upon complete Mn depletion, matching the observed low precipitate concentration in the Mn-depleted zone.
item.scope_limits: The model assumes equilibrium conditions; the authors note that experimental tests must be performed for long enough times for phase separation to occur.
item.alternatives_considered: The idea that the alloy remains a stable single-phase FCC solid solution under these conditions.
quotes: CALPHAD calculations were used to evaluate the relationship between the Mn dissolution and the concentration of precipitates.

At 700 °C, as Mn diffuses out of the Cr 18 Mn 27 Fe 27.5 Ni 27.5 alloy, the BCC phase fraction would decrease from approximately 3.7 at.% in the original alloy to 2.8 at.% when the Mn concentration reduced to 12 at.%
These results would explain the relatively low concentration of Cr-rich precipitate in the Mn-depleted zone shown in Fig. 6 .

item.mechanism: High diffusivity of Mn at 700 °C allows for a steady supply of Mn to the salt-alloy interface, enabling continuous sacrificial protection of Cr.
item.operating_conditions: High temperature (700 °C) in molten FLiBe salt
item.supporting_observation: The authors contrast this with aqueous systems where Mn diffusivity is too slow to prevent Cr reaction, noting that at 700 °C, Mn diffusivity is significantly increased.
item.scope_limits: This mechanism is temperature-dependent and would not function effectively at low temperatures where Mn diffusivity is limited.
item.alternatives_considered: Sacrificial protection in aqueous systems where Mn is added as a pure bar in electrical contact, which fails due to limited diffusivity.
quotes: However, at high temperatures such as 700 °C, the test temperature in our study, Mn diffusivity is significantly increased such that a steady supply of Mn to the salt-alloy interface is more likely to prevent significant amount of Cr atoms from reacting with the salt.
Indeed, sacrificial alloying is not a successful corrosion protection method in aqueous systems due to the limited diffusivity of elements at low temperatures
The combination of lower standard Gibbs free energy and high diffusion coefficient of Mn relative to Cr, led to the higher dissolution rate of Mn in the salt that hinder the dissolution of Cr.

item.mechanism: The formation of a Mn/MnF2 redox couple in the salt acts as a buffer that fixes the electrochemical potential of the immersed sample, preventing Cr dissolution.
item.operating_conditions: Exposure to molten FLiBe salt at 700 °C for 1000 hours
item.supporting_observation: The authors suggest that the presence of Mn in the salt creates a buffer level where Cr becomes noble, similar to techniques used in the MSR experiment by adding Mg, Zr, and Be.
item.scope_limits: The authors state it is not known how much Mn in the salt is required to reach a satisfactory buffer level.
item.alternatives_considered: The use of external metallic elements (Mg, Zr, Be) added to the salt to act as a redox buffer.
quotes: Following the significant Mn dissolution from the alloy into the salt to form MnF 2 , the Mn/MnF 2 redox couple could become a salt redox buffer, and thus the immersed sample, would then be fixed at this buffer level.
Such technique, in principle, was employed in the MSR experiment in ORNL during the 1960s by adding metallic elements such as Mg, Zr, and Be to the salt
These observations point to the possibility of using Mn/MnF 2 couple as a redox buffer to reduce the overall corrosion potential and to slow or stop the dissolution of Cr.

item.mechanism: The high entropy of mixing and sluggish diffusion hypotheses do not sufficiently explain the corrosion behavior observed, as the mechanism follows conventional thermodynamic stability rules.
item.operating_conditions: Exposure to molten FLiBe salt at 700 °C for 1000 hours
item.supporting_observation: The corrosion behavior was found to be similar to conventional alloys, controlled by thermodynamic stability of corrosion products rather than unique HEA properties.
item.scope_limits: The authors state that more experimental results with various HEAs in different salt media are needed to draw conclusions about the role of high entropy of mixing.
item.alternatives_considered: The hypothesis that HEAs possess unique corrosion resistance due to high configurational entropy and/or sluggish diffusion.
quotes: The corrosion behavior of the Cr 18 Mn 27 Fe 27.5 Ni 27.5 high entropy alloy seems to follow mechanisms observed in conventional alloys, which is controlled by the thermodynamic stability of corrosion products relative to fluorine potential and the level of impurities in the salt.
That being said, it is not sufficient to draw conclusions about the role of the high entropy of mixing and sluggish diffusion in the corrosion behavior of HEAs.
More experimental results with various HEAs in different salt media would be needed to better understand the behavior of HEAs in these corrosive environments.

item.mechanism: Precipitation of Cr-rich second phases can be beneficial for nuclear applications by immobilizing Cr, increasing high-temperature strength, and acting as defect sinks.
item.operating_conditions: In-operando conditions in MSR environment (molten salt exposure and aging at 700 °C)
item.supporting_observation: The authors argue that since Cr is immobilized as precipitates, it cannot dissolve in the salt and remains available to prevent air oxidation on the outer surface.
item.scope_limits: This benefit is contingent on the specific precipitation behavior observed; the authors note that phase separation was not reported in previous studies of this alloy.
item.alternatives_considered: The view that second phase precipitation is purely detrimental to alloy stability.
quotes: At these levels, this precipitation could be beneficial to nuclear applications.
Indeed, second phase precipitates may increase the high-temperature strength of the alloy.

Finally, since Cr is immobilized as precipitates in the surface regions beneath the alloy/salt interface, it could not potentially dissolve in the salt and would still be available at levels sufficient to prevent air oxidation on the outer side of the piping.
